messages:
Eli: Hey team — first week here. Following the new‑hire doc but hitting PATH issues on my M2 Mac. Installed Homebrew under /opt/homebrew, asdf is installed, but when I try `asdf install ruby 3.1.2` it fails because the build can't find openssl. brew works in Terminal but not in fish launched from VSCode. Anyone seen this?

Jordana: welcome! For arm64 Homebrew the default prefix is /opt/homebrew. In fish you need to add `set -x PATH /opt/homebrew/bin $PATH` to ~/.config/fish/config.fish so non-login shells (like the VSCode integrated terminal) pick it up. Also make sure `brew --prefix` is on PATH.

Amin: +1. If asdf compile needs openssl, you often need the LDFLAGS/CPPFLAGS env vars pointing at brew's openssl. Example I keep in dotfiles: ```bash export LDFLAGS="-L/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@1.1/lib" export CPPFLAGS="-I/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@1.1/include" export PKG_CONFIG_PATH="/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@1.1/lib/pkgconfig" ``` On fish that becomes `set -x LDFLAGS '-L/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@1.1/lib'` etc.

Eli: Thanks — converted the flags to fish syntax and re-ran. Now hitting a gpg key error when installing nodejs via asdf (nodejs plugin).

Jordana: For nodejs plugin we usually run the plugin's key import step: `bash ~/.asdf/plugins/nodejs/bin/import-release-team-keyring` — that calls gpg. If your gpg is the macos builtin it can be flaky; we recommend gpg installed via brew. Also check `gpgconf --list-dir` if keys not found. Our dotfiles repo has a mac-arm note: https://git.internal/redwood/dotfiles/blob/main/mac-arm.md — includes a few snippets that helped me.

Amin: Another gotcha: VSCode devcontainer/Remote might not inherit your login shell env. If you're using the Remote containers extension, make sure the shell is configured to fish and that config.fish exports the brew path early. For SSH agent + 1Password: do you plan to use the 1Password SSH agent or a local ssh-agent?

Eli: Trying to use 1Password CLI for keys (we keep keys in 1Password). VSCode couldn't forward the agent, so the git push failed. Is there a recommended flow to persist 1Password auth across shells/devcontainer?

Amin: We typically do `eval "$(op signin --sh)"` in the interactive shell so OP_SESSION env var exists. For agent-based flow: start ssh-agent, then `op item get <ssh-key-item> --attributes privateKey | ssh-add -`. There is also the official 1Password ssh integration; docs: https://1password.com/ssh. If you need a persistent agent in the devcontainer, we put a small helper in dotfiles: `scripts/op-ssh-agent.sh` that handles sign-in + add. Ping me and I can share it.

Jordana: And if you're using direnv, don't forget to add `eval (direnv hook fish)` to config.fish. Otherwise .envrc won't auto-load and you may miss LDFLAGS when switching projects.

Eli: Good call — I'm using direnv for per‑project envs. One more thing: asdf + fish init — I couldn't get `asdf` command available in fish until I sourced the asdf script in config.fish. Any recommended line?

Amin: In fish I add: `source (asdf where)/asdf.fish` — or if installed via Homebrew it might be at `/opt/homebrew/opt/asdf/libexec/asdf.fish`. Our dotfiles set a wrapper that detects sys prefix; if you want I can paste the exact snippet.

Eli: Node gpg error fixed after installing gpg via brew and running the import script. SSH agent still a pain inside the container; I'll try Amin's helper. Thanks for the quick tips! :raised_hands:

Jordana: welcome aboard! If anything still blocks you, @onboarding or drop logs in #help and tag me.

devbot: onboarding reminder — see https://handbook.redwood.com/onboarding for dev environment checklist.
